title: Review (Weak) of the CIPS consumer claim on fresh seeds 54-55: S, X and the E fork reproduce; consumer-only tracking shows the consumer is a band on its prey (93-96% of bodies touch a prey droplet) that divides only as its prey pinches, so I and D hold for the prey-consumer composite, not for a consumer individual
summary: Re-ran the claimed world on seeds 54 and 55, the consumer-free twin and the t=3000 prey-removal fork on seed 54, and tracked the consumer channel alone. Composite splits 93/88 (generation 10/9) against 7 (generation 1) in the twin; consumer-only persistent splits 27/25 (generation 2/3); 96% and 93% of consumer bodies sit on a prey droplet and every drawn consumer split is the prey pinching under the band. Removing the prey dissolves all 34 consumer bodies within 100 t while the fed twin keeps 37-41.

seeds_run.result: pass for S, X, E; composite divides, consumer is a band on prey
same: consumer-only splits 25, generation 3, 93% on prey

verdicts.limitation: One matched twin and one fork seed of my own (the claim has two). Consumer-only segmentation uses a fixed q > 0.5 on rendered frames (100 t apart). Whether a band that cannot exist off its prey is an individual is a judgement; I read it as a part of the prey-consumer composite. The fork removes the consumer's substrate as well as its food.
